title: Senior Manager, Sales and Customer Success
description:
Clubspeed & Resova
Build the team. Create the playbook. Scale the customer revenue engine.
Clubspeed and Resova provide venue management, booking, and payments technology to experience-based businesses around the world.
We’re entering an exciting new chapter. With new investment behind the business, we’re building the teams, systems, and operating rhythms needed to accelerate growth while delivering a consistently strong experience for our customers.
We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Sales & Customer Success to lead that transformation across our customer segments.
The Opportunity
This is not a role where you inherit a fully built sales and customer success machine.
You’ll have the opportunity to help build it.
You’ll lead and develop a growing team responsible for customer retention, expansion, and new revenue while creating the processes, playbooks, metrics, and management structure required to operate effectively at scale.
The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. One day you may be designing the customer segmentation model or renewal process; the next, you may be coaching a rep through an expansion opportunity, reviewing an at-risk account, or helping close a deal.
You’ll have meaningful ownership over how we serve and grow our SMB and Mid-Market customers—and the opportunity to build a function that can scale with the business.
What Success Looks Like
In this role, you will:
Build a high-performing SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success organization with clear roles, expectations, KPIs, and accountability.
Recruit, onboard, coach, and develop a strong team of Account Managers and Customer Success professionals.
Create scalable customer journeys and playbooks across onboarding, adoption, retention, renewal, and expansion.
Improve Net Revenue Retention by reducing preventable churn and creating a consistent expansion motion across the customer base.
Establish clear forecasting and pipeline management for renewals, upsells, cross-sells, and other customer revenue opportunities.
Introduce a scalable operating model that balances high-touch engagement for strategic customers with efficient 1-to-many programs for SMB customers.
Build better visibility into customer health, revenue risk, and expansion potential.
Create a disciplined, accountable culture where the team understands what great performance looks like and has the coaching and tools to achieve it.
What You’ll DoKey Responsibilities
Lead, Build & Develop the Team
Lead the SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success teams, establishing clear expectations, responsibilities, and performance standards.
Own recruiting and hiring as the organization grows.
Build structured onboarding and enablement programs that help new team members ramp quickly.
Conduct regular 1:1s, pipeline reviews, account reviews, and call coaching.
Develop the team’s capabilities in consultative selling, negotiation, customer relationship management, retention, and expansion.
Establish clear individual and team KPIs and create a strong culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
Identify performance gaps early and coach team members toward stronger outcomes.
Build the Customer Success Operating Model
Design and document scalable playbooks for onboarding, adoption, account management, renewal, expansion, and churn prevention.
Develop differentiated engagement models for SMB and Mid-Market customers based on customer value, complexity, opportunity, and risk.
Build repeatable 1-to-many programs that allow the team to effectively support a high-volume customer base.
Establish customer health scoring and early-warning indicators for churn and expansion opportunities.
Define clear escalation paths and operating processes across Sales, Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Product, and Payments.
Continuously identify opportunities to simplify workflows and improve team productivity.
Drive Retention & Expansion
Own the team’s performance against Net Revenue Retention, renewal, churn, and expansion targets.
Establish a consistent renewal process that creates visibility well in advance of contract expiration.
Build and standardize upsell and cross-sell motions across the customer base.
Coach the team on identifying customer needs, creating value-based expansion opportunities, and successfully navigating commercial conversations.
Partner with internal teams to address customer risks before they become churn events.
Step into strategic or complex customer conversations when leadership involvement can materially improve the outcome.
Create Revenue Visibility & Accountability
Build accurate weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasting for renewals, expansion, and customer revenue.
Establish pipeline standards and operating rhythms that give leadership a clear view of expected performance.
Track and analyze performance metrics across the customer lifecycle.
Use product usage, customer engagement, commercial, and CRM data to identify risks and opportunities.
Ensure CRM and Customer Success systems accurately reflect account activity, pipeline, customer health, and next steps.
Provide leadership with clear insights into performance, trends, risks, and opportunities.
You’ll Thrive Here If...
You enjoy building structure where it doesn’t yet exist.
You believe strong leadership means both setting a clear standard and actively coaching people toward it.
You like working close to customers and are comfortable getting involved when an important account or opportunity needs help.
You are commercially minded and view Customer Success as an important driver of revenue, not simply a support function.
You are comfortable being accountable to clear metrics and expect the same from your team.
You can identify what needs to be standardized without adding unnecessary process.
You enjoy working in an environment where the business is evolving quickly and you can directly influence how the function develops.
You are excited by the opportunity to build something that is expected to become significantly larger over time.
Why Join Clubspeed?
This is an opportunity to join a category-leading business at an important stage of its growth.
We have an established customer base, proven products, and significant industry expertise—and we’re investing in building a stronger, more scalable commercial organization around them.
You’ll have the opportunity to:
Build and shape a critical customer-facing function.
Hire and develop your own team.
Influence how we segment, serve, retain, and grow our customers.
Work directly with company leadership on revenue strategy and execution.
Create systems and playbooks that become the foundation for future scale.
Have a measurable impact on customer retention, expansion, and company growth.
What You’ll Get
Significant ownership and autonomy over the SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success organization.
The opportunity to build rather than simply maintain an existing function.
A seat at the table and meaningful influence over company strategy.
A growing organization where strong performers can expand their scope as the business scales.
The ability to make a visible impact on customers, employees, and company performance.
Our Hiring Process
Our hiring process is designed to be straightforward and conversational.
We want to understand how you think, how you lead, what you’ve built before, and how you would approach scaling a customer-facing revenue organization.
You’ll also have the opportunity to meet members of the leadership team, learn more about where Clubspeed and Resova are headed, and determine whether this is the right environment for you.
Join UsIf you’re excited by the opportunity to build a team, create scalable commercial processes, develop great people, and directly influence retention and growth, we’d love to hear from you.
What We’re Looking For
5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, or a related commercial function.
2+ years of direct people management or team leadership experience.
Demonstrated success hiring, onboarding, coaching, and developing customer-facing teams.
Experience operating in a high-volume SMB and/or Mid-Market environment.
Strong commercial instincts with experience managing renewals, expansion opportunities, contract negotiations, and revenue targets.
Proven ability to build processes, playbooks, operating cadences, or functions rather than simply working within established ones.
Strong understanding of Customer Success metrics including Net Revenue Retention, Gross Revenue Retention, churn, expansion, renewal rates, and customer health.
Strong forecasting, pipeline management, and performance management capabilities.
Experience using CRM and Customer Success platforms to improve visibility, automation, and team effectiveness.
Comfort working with data and translating performance metrics into concrete actions.
Ability to move between strategic planning and hands-on execution.
Competitive base+bonus compensation structure
Comprehensive health coverage, including dental and vision
Flexible time off policy

title: Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
description:
Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 
Are you actively looking for a new opportunity? Or just checking the market? Well… you might just be in the right place!
As the Senior Manager, Revenue Operations, you will lead two critical global pillars for Lightspeed: our Sales & Partner Commissions engine and the RevOps Capital GTM optimization & performance function. On the incentives side, you will own the end-to-end strategy, design, governance, and continuous optimization of all sales and partner commission programs, ensuring they are simple, scalable, compliant, and tightly aligned with our growth and profitability goals—while leading high-performing analyst teams to deliver accurate, timely, and trusted execution. On the RevOps Capital side, you will operate as the GTM performance “control tower,” driving forecasting, KPI frameworks, quota and coverage analytics, and weekly/monthly/quarterly business reviews that translate data into clear recommendations on investment, productivity, and commercial optimization. Partnering closely with RevOps, Finance, GTM, Legal, Enablement, and Information Systems leadership, you will ensure that every dollar we deploy in commissions and Capital programs is intentional, measurable, and focused on accelerating sustainable revenue growth and seller/partner performance globally.
 What you’ll be doing: 
 Part 1 – Global Sales & Partner Commissions 
 Program strategy, design & analytics: Own the global design, governance, and continuous improvement of sales and partner commission frameworks, using deep quantitative analysis, scenario modeling, and performance data to ensure incentives are simple, scalable, and tightly aligned with growth and profitability goals.
 Commission operations, systems & scalability: Lead end-to-end commission execution for sales and partners, ensuring payouts are accurate, timely, and aligned with contracts and plan documents; drive the transition from manual processes to scalable systems and tools, embedding robust controls, automation, and data quality.
 Insights, GTM impact & executive reporting: Turn commission and performance data into actionable insights for GTM leaders, highlighting behavioral trends, risks, and opportunities; own monthly executive readouts and presentations, delivering clear narratives and recommendations grounded in data.
 Stakeholder management & change leadership: Act as the primary RevOps point of contact for Sales, Partnerships, Finance, Legal, and IS on incentive topics; lead cross-functional changes to plan design, tooling, and processes, managing communication, enablement, and adoption across regions and teams.
 Team leadership & development: Manage, coach, and develop Sales and Partner Commissions Analysts, setting clear priorities, KPIs, and quality standards while fostering a high-performance, detail-oriented culture focused on accuracy, accountability, insights, and continuous improvement.
 Part 2 – RevOps Capital (Planning, Reporting & Performance) 
 Forecasting & reforecasting: Lead the end-to-end forecasting and reforecasting cadence for the Capital business (EOM, EOQ, EOY), refining assumptions with GTM and Finance based on macro trends, pipeline quality, and performance.
 Quota, coverage & capacity modeling: Drive quota-setting, coverage, and capacity models for Capital GTM roles, providing data-backed recommendations that align with company targets, TAM, and productivity benchmarks.
 Performance cadence (WBR/MBR/QBR): Own the weekly, monthly, and quarterly performance review cadence for Capital, bringing a “control tower” view of pipeline, bookings, portfolio metrics, and rep-level performance, and turning insights into clear actions with GTM leadership.
 KPI frameworks & strategic planning: Define and evolve KPI frameworks to measure Capital health and efficiency across the lifecycle, and translate insights into recommendations on where to invest, optimize, and improve unit economics.
 Cross-functional alignment & communication: Partner with Product, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Risk, and Enablement to align Capital GTM plans and reporting with company priorities; communicate complex analyses and options in clear, executive-ready narratives.
 Team & capability building: Build and mature RevOps Capital analytical capabilities, defining ways of working, tooling, and best practices, while coaching team members to strengthen strategic thinking, business acumen, and influence with senior stakeholders.
 What you need to bring: 
8-10 years in SaaS or technology, ideally in Revenue Operations, Finance, or related GTM operations roles. 4+ years of people management experience leading high-performing analytical teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting or related field; Master’s is a plus.
Strong background in incentive compensation and sales/partner commissions, from design and modeling to operational execution.
Hands-on experience with forecasting, planning, and performance management in partnership with Finance and GTM leadership.
Highly analytical, process-oriented, and detail-focused, with experience using systems/tools (commission platforms, CRM, BI) to scale operations.
Excellent communication and executive presence, with a track record of presenting insights and recommendations to senior leadership; experience in Financial Services or Capital products is a plus.
As a global company with employees and clients outside of Quebec, fluency in English as a working language is required for this position
 What will make you successful: 
 Exceptional analytical & quantitative skills: You’re comfortable deep in spreadsheets, models, and dashboards, turning complex performance and commission data into clear, actionable insights.
 Strategic systems thinker: You can zoom out to design scalable frameworks for incentives, forecasting, and performance management, while staying close enough to the details to spot risks and edge cases.
 Clear, confident communicator: You can explain complex commission logic, trade-offs, and Capital performance insights to executives and front-line teams in simple, compelling language.
 Change leadership & influence: You’re skilled at driving adoption of new plans, tools, and processes across GTM, Finance, Legal, and IS, building buy-in rather than just enforcing rules.
 Operator mindset & bias for action: You care about accuracy and control, but you also move fast—constantly looking for ways to streamline, automate, and improve how the work gets done.
 Collaborative team player: You build strong relationships across functions and regions, balancing partner/revenue goals with governance, compliance, and operational feasibility.
 People leadership & talent development: You enjoy coaching analytical talent, setting clear expectations, giving feedback, and building a high-performance culture grounded in ownership and accountability.
We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try!
 Be a changemaker 
You’ll enjoy:
A flexible work environment that empowers you to do your best work
A culture that celebrates performance
The chance to make an impact in a team that’s big enough for career growth, but lean enough to make your voice heard
Career-defining opportunities
Plus benefits designed to keep you happy, healthy and fulfilled.
Flexible paid time off and remote work policies
Equity options, because this is your company too
Contributions to your pension plan. Your future matters
Training opportunities to grow your skills and career
Health and wellness credit so you feel your best
Time off to volunteer and give back to your community
Interest groups, employee led networks, social committees to sponsored sports teams
Computer purchase program to get your personal Macbook
Enhanced parental leave to support growing families
Fuel your growth. Find your people.
At Lightspeed, your growth is our priority. We invest in you with continuous learning opportunities, global mobility and benefits designed to support you—all within a driven, diverse and inclusive team that’s passionate about empowering our communities

 #LI-TL2
 To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. 
 Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. 
 Where to from here? 
Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.
Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.
 Who we are: 
Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks.
Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.
Lightspeed handles your information in accordance with our Applicant Privacy Statement.

title: Head of Customer Success & Onboarding
description:
Purpose of role: The Head of Customer Onboarding & Success will lead the onboarding of new customers onto the Ezora financial control and analytics solution and to ensure that existing customers continue to receive the full benefits of the Ezora service. This is a remote working role, based in Ireland, with occasional travel to company events or meetings.
 Please note applications must apply via this link: https://ezora.hirehive.com/head-of-customer-onboarding-success-dublin-ezekma
 About Ezora 
Ezora is a scaling Irish SaaS company that has built an innovative financial control and analytics platform. As part of our solution, we integrate with a number of systems from some of the largest brands in the Food & Beverage and Retail sectors, including McDonald's, Burger King, KFC, Starbucks, Costa, and M&S.
The Ezora platform ingests, validates, and reconciles operational and financial data into a single verified source of truth, automating up to 95% of customers' monthly accounting entries. Coupled with that, our analytics layer provides bespoke metrics, visualisations and reports that key decision-makers in these brands use to run their companies on a daily basis.
On top of this verified data, Ezora also enables AI-powered analysis, letting customers connect their own data securely to a leading AI model and interrogate their numbers in plain language, with the model reasoning only over data that has already been validated and reconciled.
 Why this role exists 
Ezora is growing its customer base of QSR and retail franchise operators, and our ability to deliver new implementations and manage existing client relationships needs to scale with it. As we grow, we need a dedicated owner for client communication and project coordination, someone who can give every project a single, consistent owner from kickoff through to go-live and beyond.
You'll become the day-to-day owner of every customer implementation and project at Ezora - the person who knows what's happening, when, and why, across every live engagement. You'll be the connective tissue between our customers, our CEO, our delivery teams, and any third parties involved, making sure nothing falls through the cracks and every customer feels looked after.
This is a foundational hire for Ezora. Done well, it directly improves how fast we get paid for the work we've sold, how happy our customers are, and how much founder time is freed up for growth.
 What you'll do In your first 6 months, the priority is delivery and communication
Own the project plan for every new customer implementation: timelines, milestones, deliverables, resourcing, and dependencies.
Be the primary point of contact for customers during implementation and ongoing delivery.
Track every open project in the business at any given time, and be able to answer "what's the status of X" without needing to ask anyone else.
Coordinate everyone involved in getting a project over the line - the customer, third parties, our internal business teams, and our tech team.
Work closely with the leads of our data, analytics, and finance functions to plan and sequence delivery work realistically.
Identify and flag risk early: projects stalling, unclear scope, missing information, or customers going quiet.
Build and maintain a simple, reliable way for the leadership team to see project status across the whole book at a glance.
As you settle into the role, this expands into customer success
Take ownership of customer success for key accounts: proactively checking in, understanding how customers are using Ezora, and spotting risk or opportunity before it becomes urgent.
Build relationships with customer stakeholders beyond the implementation team, so Ezora has more than one point of contact within each account.
Represent the voice of the customer internally - feeding insight back into product, delivery process, and how we sell.
Help define what "customer success" looks like at Ezora as we grow: what we measure, how we check in, and how we catch problems before they become churn.
 What we're looking for 
Industry background. You've worked in or closely with QSR, hospitality, retail, or franchise operations - you understand the operational and financial pressures our customers face, and you can speak their language from day one.
Empathy and customer instinct. You can genuinely see things from the customer's point of view, even when it's inconvenient for us. You advocate for the customer and ensure they get what they need.
Excellent communication. You can talk to a franchise operator, a finance team, and a developer in the same week and be clearly understood by all three. You write clearly, you don't let things go unsaid, and you're comfortable delivering difficult updates as well as good news.
Highly organised. You naturally track multiple moving parts without dropping any of them. You bring structure and visibility to things that are currently informal.
Financial literacy, financial systems & data systems. You have a strong understanding of financial systems, restaurant or retail systems and strong reporting and analytical skills.
A track record of delivery. You've run projects that involved coordinating multiple groups - internal teams, customers, third parties - to hit a deadline or outcome. You know how to build a realistic plan and hold people (including yourself) to it.
Seniority and scope. You've operated at a senior level before - leading a delivery, project management, or client services function, not just contributing to one. You're comfortable owning outcomes across a whole portfolio of projects and pushing back when priorities or resourcing don't add up.
Comfortable with ambiguity early on. This role doesn't have a well-worn playbook at Ezora yet. You'll help build the process as well as run it.
No specific qualifications are required. We care much more about relevant experience and evidence of the traits above than about formal credentials. Project management certifications (PMP, PRINCE2, Agile/Scrum) are a plus but not a requirement.
 What success looks like 
Every open project has a clear plan, owner, and status that anyone on the leadership team can check at any time.
Closed contracts move to live/billing faster and more predictably, with far fewer projects stalling for reasons within our control.
Customers feel they have a consistent, reliable relationship with Ezora - someone who knows their context and follows through.
Over time, you own a clear view of customer health across our key accounts, and can speak confidently to how happy each of them is with Ezora.

description:
About Us
 Climate Impact Partners is the trusted partner for organizations taking ambitious climate action. Since 1997, we’ve helped leading businesses reduce or remove more than 151 million tonnes of CO₂e, turning climate ambition into measurable results.
We deliver high-quality carbon market solutions: developing and financing impactful projects, managing carbon credit and energy attribute certificate portfolios, and helping companies put a price on carbon to drive change.
By connecting corporates, governments, innovators, and project partners, we accelerate investment in climate solutions that deliver verified impact and advance progress toward net-zero goals.
 What Sets Us Apart
 Boundless, urgent ambition. We are accountable, relentless, resilient.
 Courage to innovate. We are courageous, creative, curious.
 Integrity without compromise. We are trustworthy, credible, committed.
 Empowered to serve. We are respectful, inclusive, collaborative.
 THE ROLE
 We are seeking a Revenue Operations Analyst to join our Revenue Operations team.
In this role, you will support the analysis and improvement of our sales and marketing funnel—bringing structure, visibility, and insights to our GTM reporting. You’ll collaborate closely with sales, finance, digital, and leadership teams to understand performance drivers, help spot where performance is slipping, and make sure revenue-generating teams have accurate data to operate effectively.
We are looking for a strong analyst first. You will bring the technical craft; we will teach you the commercial context of the carbon markets we operate in.
You will work closely with the Revenue Operations Associate Director, who sets direction for the function and will coach you through the work. This is a role built for someone early in their revenue operations career, with clear scope to take on broader ownership as you grow.
 Responsibilities
 Sales Funnel Analytics
Analyze performance across the full GTM funnel—from lead generation through deal close and revenue recognition—to surface insights and conversion trends.
Track and optimize key metrics (e.g., lead-to-opportunity rate, opportunity-to-close rate, sales cycle length, pipeline velocity).
Build and maintain dashboards and reports (e.g., in Salesforce, Excel, Power BI, web-based reports) to support visibility and decision-making.
Provide weekly/monthly reporting on KPIs, pipeline health, sales productivity, and attainment against targets.
Segment performance by rep, region, and product to uncover opportunities for coaching or reallocation.
Support sales leadership in pipeline hygiene efforts to ensure accuracy and forecasting confidence.
Track new business vs. expansion funnels so the team can see where to focus effort.
 Process & System Optimization
Identify gaps, inconsistencies, or inefficiencies in data and work cross-functionally to resolve them.
Partner with sales leadership to streamline processes for lead handoffs, opportunity stages, and pipeline tracking.
Support implementation of sales methodologies and keep CRM workflows aligned to agreed sales processes.
Partner with Enablement to identify performance gaps and inform training priorities using data.
Participate in GTM retrospectives to assess what’s working and where pivots are needed.
Collaborate with RevOps, Finance and Digital to ensure data cleanliness, CRM alignment, and accurate forecasting inputs.
Suggest automation that reduces manual data entry and saves the sales team time.
Use AI tools (including Claude and Claude Code) to accelerate analysis, reporting, and documentation — partnering with the Digital team, who own our AI tooling and core platforms (Salesforce, D365, Business Central), and following agreed governance and workflows.
 Strategic Planning & Forecasting Support
Prepare the data and analysis that feeds quarterly business reviews and go-to-market planning.
Analyze historical trends to inform future revenue and funnel performance projections.
Work with sales leadership to understand rep performance drivers, ramp timelines, and capacity planning needs.
Pull and prepare the historical conversion data used in territory planning and quota setting.
Flag early when pipeline coverage, conversion trends or sales velocity drift from plan.
Work with FP&A on the inputs behind revenue forecasts and financial reporting cadences.
 What We Are Looking For
 Experience and Skills
1–3 years in a GTM analytics, sales/marketing operations, or RevOps role — or a strong analytical grounding in another field and the appetite to move into RevOps
Strong in Excel or Google Sheets — able to clean messy data and build an analysis from scratch, not just maintain someone else’s
A builder: you have built reports or dashboards yourself in a BI tool such as Power BI, Looker or Tableau
Hands-on with a CRM (Salesforce or similar) and with AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to speed up analysis and build
Digs for the root cause rather than reporting the symptom, and brings a proposed solution alongside the problem
Able to write up what you found clearly enough for a non-technical reader to act on it
 What We’ll Coach You On
Judgment on which questions matter most commercially, and where your time is best spent
Presenting to senior leaders in the terms they care about — leading with the decision, not the method
Working in the open with sales, finance and digital — testing your thinking with them rather than analyzing in a bubble
How our B2B funnel, KPIs and carbon-market commercial model actually work
 Personal Attributes
Organized and self-directed — able to juggle several priorities and hit deadlines without being chased.
Keen to learn, with an appetite for feedback — you will get direct coaching from the Revenue Operations Associate Director and broad exposure to how a commercial team runs.

The Commercial Strategy & Planning team plays a pivotal role in driving our strategic power plays by shaping, orchestrating, and driving the commercial strategy that underpins our growth ambitions. It is cross-functional, fast-paced and we work on Amex GBT’s most challenging strategic projects, delivering for senior stakeholders.
This role focuses on the ‘Go Big on SME’ and ‘Champion Customer Obsession’ powerplays, giving you exposure to a wide range of functions and the opportunity to contribute to strategic initiatives that have real bottom-line impact. It's a great opportunity for someone early in their strategy career to build broad commercial and analytical skills while working alongside experienced practitioners.
 What you'll do: 
Support senior colleagues in developing and delivering the organisation's long-term corporate strategy, contributing research, analysis and structured recommendations.
Help prepare high-quality presentations, briefing documents and materials for senior leadership and key business stakeholders.
Act as a day-to-day point of contact for departments across the organisation, spanning Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Strategy, Finance, and Product, providing commercial insight and analytical support.
Contribute to cross-functional strategic projects, working collaboratively across commercial, operational, and corporate teams under the guidance of a project lead.
Build strong working relationships with stakeholders across the business, developing your ability to influence and communicate effectively in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment.
Help gather and organise customer insights and feedback so they can be embedded into strategy formulation, ensuring our offerings stay aligned with customer needs.
Support work to evolve our commercial operating model (people, process, and technology), helping to document current processes and identify opportunities for improvement.
 What we're looking for: 
3+ years of experience in commercial strategy, business planning, go-to-market, or a related analytical role, or a consultancy/graduate scheme background; ideally with exposure to B2B or a similar strategic environment.
Good commercial awareness with an ability to turn data and analysis into clear, structured insights.
A highly analytical, structured thinker with strong problem-solving skills and a data-driven approach.
Some experience working with stakeholders across different business functions, with a genuine interest in developing your influencing and relationship-building skills.
Exposure to, or interest in, cross-functional projects involving people, process, or technology change.
A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to manage your own workload and contribute confidently to fast-moving pieces of work.
Strong communication and presentation skills, with the confidence to engage colleagues from operational teams through to senior stakeholders.
Familiarity with commercial governance frameworks, operating models, or performance dashboards is a plus.
An interest in AI, automation, or digital tools for sales and marketing transformation is preferred.
 Location 
London, United Kingdom
 The #TeamGBT Experience 
Work and life: Find your happy medium at Amex GBT.
 Flexible benefits are tailored to each country and start the day you do. These include health and welfare insurance plans, retirement programs, parental leave, adoption assistance, and wellbeing resources to support you and your immediate family.
 Travel perks: get a choice of deals each week from major travel providers on everything from flights to hotels to cruises and car rentals.
 Develop the skills you want when the time is right for you, with access to over 20,000 courses on our learning platform, leadership courses, and new job openings available to internal candidates first.
 We strive to champion Inclusion in every aspect of our business at Amex GBT. You can connect with colleagues through our global INclusion Groups, centered around common identities or initiatives, to discuss challenges, obstacles, achievements, and drive company awareness and action.
And much more!
All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to age, sex, gender (and characteristics related to sex and gender), pregnancy (and related medical conditions), race, color, citizenship, religion, disability, or any other class or characteristic protected by law.
Click Here for Additional Disclosures in Accordance with the LA County Fair Chance Ordinance.
Furthermore, we are committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities. Please let your recruiter know if you need an accommodation at any point during the hiring process. For details regarding how we protect your data, please consult the Amex GBT Recruitment Privacy Statement.
 What if I don’t meet every requirement? If you’re passionate about our mission and believe you’d be a phenomenal addition to our team, don’t worry about “checking every box;" please apply anyway. You may be exactly the person we’re looking for!

This flexibility enables our customers to achieve their highest-priority goals faster. And because Tines is secure and private by design, it’s popular with security, IT, engineering, finance, and other security-focused teams.
At Tines, we're driven by our values of Simplicity, Speed, and Soundness. We're committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences while fostering a company culture that nurtures individual curiosity, growth, and integrity. We’re excited about what’s next, and we’re looking for others to join us on our journey.
We're looking for a sales compensation leader to own how we pay our go-to-market organisation, and how that changes as our commercial model changes. You will run the engine that pays roughly 350 GTM people accurately and on time, own the design of the plans, quotas and incentives behind it, and lead a small team of analysts.
The timing is the interesting part. Tines is moving from subscription and seat-based pricing to a consumption model, which means designing and running two comp worlds in parallel while we transition. At the same time we are rebuilding the quote-to-cash stack on Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced, which resets crediting and the data that feeds it. You will be central to both.
This is a hands-on leadership role. You will manage and coach a small team, and you will also be in the model, in CaptivateIQ, and in the plan documents yourself.
 What You'll be Doing: 
 Run the compensation engine 
Own the monthly and quarterly compensation cycle end to end: crediting, calculation, review, approval and payout, delivered accurately and on time
Own CaptivateIQ as our system of record for incentive compensation, including plan build, rule logic, testing and release
Own crediting and comp data integrity across Salesforce and downstream systems, and work with Systems and Deal Desk to fix problems at source rather than in spreadsheets
Oversee inquiry management ensuring clear SLAs and report on trends to improve overall processes
Document and keep policies and process up to date for stakeholders and your team
 Design the plans, quotas and incentives 
Own annual plan design in partnership with your Senior compensation analyst, GTM leadership, FP&A and People for all commissioned roles
Collaborate with Revops business partners on the quota setting process for each function to ensure it aligns with broader compensation strategy and benchmarks
Model attainment distribution, benchmarks and support finance in ad-hoc cost reporting
Own and build SPIFFs and non-cash incentive programmes, including President's Club,
Own plan communication and enablement, so reps and managers understand what they are paid for and can self-serve where needed
 Evolve The Compensation Strategy As We Grow 
Build the compensation approach for an evolving pricing model and mulit-product business in partnership with the Head of Revenue Operations and VP of Finance
Represent compensation requirements during larger CPQ and CRM enhancements or changes
Enhance our approach based compensation reporting: attainment by role and segment, payout curves, quota coverage and programme effectiveness
 Lead and grow the team 
Manage, coach and develop a small team of compensation analysts, and set the standard and what good looks like
Prioritise the team's work, capacity and quarterly OKRs to ensure a balance of reactiveness and impactful projects
Stay hands-on. This is a doing and leading role, not a management-only role
 What you bring with you: 
6+ years in sales compensation, revenue operations, sales finance or a closely related field, with experience managing or formally mentoring analysts
2-3 years direct management experience
Proven ownership of a full incentive compensation cycle for a distributed GTM team, including crediting, calculation, payout and dispute resolution
Hands-on administration of an ICM platform, ideally CaptivateIQ, including building and testing plan logic yourself

Strong Salesforce data fluency, and the ability to translate commercial requirements into system and crediting logic
Advanced Excel or Google Sheets modelling, including capacity, attainment and cost of sale models

You can communicate simply, clearly, and directly, especially with senior leaders, and your written work is polished enough to go straight to an executive audience
 Bonus points

Experience in cybersecurity, IT or AI markets

title: Head of Strategy and Business Operations
description:
About InvestEngine 
InvestEngine is everything the modern investor should need. Unbeatable value, market-leading automation, and built for easy, long-term investing. We've built a strong foundation, have over £3 billion invested, award-winning service, and a passionate team — now we're ready to scale. We are seeking a hands-on Head of Strategy & Business Operations to partner with our CEO in setting the strategic agenda, running the company and building the operating model that will carry us through the next stage of growth.
 About The Role 
As Head of Strategy & Business Operations, you will operate at the intersection of strategy, operations and executive decision-making, combining analytical judgement with hands-on execution. You will work closely with the CEO as part of a lean leadership team, leading the Strategy & Business Operations function and a team of five.
You will translate high-level objectives into clear execution plans, operating rhythms, KPIs and measurable outcomes, acting as an integrator who drives delivery across every function in the business rather than managing a large team of your own. This is a newly created role: much of the framework you will run does not yet exist in a formal shape, and building it is a core part of the job.
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Operating Model & Company Rhythm 
Design and run InvestEngine's company operating model, including the goal cycle, executive meeting architecture, business reviews and decision governance.
Own the quarterly goal cycle end to end, working with function leaders to set targets that are ambitious, measurable and owned.
Run the executive cadence so that decisions are made once, documented and acted upon, and surface risks and slippage early.
 Strategy & Planning 
Own the annual and multi-year strategic planning process, from framing the agenda to a plan the leadership team commits to.
Partner with the CEO and leadership team on strategic planning, prioritisation and resource allocation.
Structure and answer the company's most significant open questions, including market sizing, prioritisation and build-versus-buy decisions.
Bring an independent, evidence-based point of view to executive discussions, including where it differs from the prevailing one.
 Cross-Functional Delivery 
Own the portfolio of company-wide initiatives, with clear prioritisation and formal start and stop gates.
Lead high-impact initiatives end to end, resolving delivery challenges directly rather than escalating them.
Embed completed work with the function that will own it as business-as-usual, leaving no residual dependency on your team.
 Performance & Reporting 
Own the monthly CEO pack and quarterly Board pack, produced from a single, trusted source of truth.
Develop the KPI framework covering commercial performance, delivery, customer outcomes, cost efficiency and operational risk.
Build the analysis yourself, working with Data & Analytics on the underlying infrastructure.
 Team Leadership 
Lead, develop and grow a team of five, setting remits, priorities and standards, and hiring into open roles.
Partner closely with leaders across Product, Technology, Platform Operations, Marketing, Data & Analytics, Finance, Compliance and People, securing outcomes from teams that do not report to you.

We are looking for an experienced and strategic leader to shape and deliver our global channel partner and sales enablement strategy. Own the end-to-end channel programme lifecycle, from strategy development and business case creation through to global rollout, adoption and value realisation.

title: Director, Growth Strategy, Planning + Ops
description:
Before TuneCore, artists needed to be signed to a record label to sell their music online. In 2006, we democratized the industry by partnering directly with digital stores and streaming platforms to enable any musician to sell their songs worldwide while retaining 100% ownership of their music. Today, TuneCore is the leading independent development partner for self-releasing artists to build audiences and careers, with technology and services across distribution, publishing administration and a range of promotional services. TuneCore is headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, and owned by Paris-based Believe, one of the world’s leading digital music companies. The company is one of the fastest growing companies in the music industry and is actively investing in the continued growth of the business. 
We have made it our mission to best serve artists and labels at each stage of their development in the digital world. We are a company that cares deeply about our people and our creator community, advocating for diversity, equity, and inclusion across all of our platforms and throughout our business. The pursuit of innovation inspires us to work hard for our artists, while collaboration drives the way we work and approach our company’s social responsibility.
Join TuneCore as we embark on the next phase of innovation in the music industry. Be part of the team that bridges the unmet and evolving needs of creators by building the tools and services that make their lives better.
 Job Description
As we evolve our product, redefine our brand and accelerate global growth, we're creating a Growth organisation capable of operating with the discipline of a world-class technology business and the creativity of a culture-leading brand for independent artists.
Reporting to the the VP Brand Marketing this role will be responsible for building the engine that powers this transformation. Acting as a strategic partner to the Leadership Team, you will establish the planning and operating model that enables Brand and Growth to operate as one high-performing global organisation that finds, retains and empowers independent artists at scale.
This is an exceptional opportunity for a highly driven, entrepreneurial leader who enjoys building from the ground up. You will design and embed the frameworks, rhythms and governance that bring clarity, alignment and accountability to how Marketing works - transforming ambition into measurable execution at scale. From annual planning and integrated campaign operations to launch excellence and budget management, you will create the systems that enable the team to move faster, make better decisions and deliver greater commercial impact.
Working closely with Product, Finance, Data, Customer Experience, regional teams and colleagues across Believe, TuneCore’s parent company, you will operationalise the creation, communication and delivery of key strategic initiatives, ensuring they are scalable, measurable and aligned to business priorities. You will champion an insight-led approach to planning, helping the organisation develop a deeper understanding of artist needs, marketing effectiveness and opportunities for growth.
You are equally comfortable shaping strategy and rolling up your sleeves to make it happen. You thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments, are naturally curious and data-driven, and bring the confidence to challenge thinking, influence senior stakeholders and continuously improve the way teams work together. Above all, you believe that operational excellence is not about process for process' sake - it exists to unlock creativity, accelerate innovation and ultimately help more independent artists succeed at scale.
 The tasks and responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:
 Strategy + Planning
Partner with Leadership to define strategic priorities, resource allocation and investment decisions. 
Develop and own the annual planning process, translating company objectives into integrated marketing priorities and measurable outcomes. 
Establish quarterly and bi-annual planning rhythms that align Growth, Brand, Product and the business teams around shared objectives. 
Build and maintain the organisation’s roadmap, ensuring visibility across initiatives, launches and campaigns. 
 Operations
Design and implement scalable operating models, governance and ways of working. 
Introduce best practice planning processes, briefing frameworks, approval workflows and project management disciplines. 
Establish clear roles, responsibilities and decision-making frameworks across the organisation. 
Drive operational excellence through continuous process improvement and simplification. 
Lead cross-functional planning, ensuring Product, Growth, Brand, Creative, Regional and Finance teams are aligned from strategy through execution. 
Create consistent launch frameworks, timelines, playbooks and retrospectives to improve delivery over time. 
 Marketing Performance & Measurement
Build the measurement framework, defining success metrics across Brand, Growth and Int’l teams. 
Develop dashboards and reporting that provide real-time, actionable visibility of performance, campaign effectiveness, pipeline contribution and business outcomes. 
Partner with Finance + Insights teams to establish attribution models, reporting standards and performance insights. 
Lead regular business reviews, identifying opportunities to optimise performance and improve return on investment. 
 Budget + Resource Management
Partner with Finance and Growth Leadership to manage annual marketing budgets and investment planning. 
Track spend across teams, markets and programmes, ensuring effective allocation of resources against strategic priorities. 
Build forecasting models and investment frameworks that support data-informed decision making. 
 Cross-functional Leadership
Act as the operational connector between Growth, Brand, Product, Finance, Data,Customer Experience and Business teams. 
Facilitate strategic planning sessions, leadership reviews and cross-functional governance meetings. 
Foster a culture of accountability, transparency and continuous improvement across the organisation. 
Some international travel (at least 10-25% of the time) is required
 Qualifications
10+ years experience in Marketing Strategy, Marketing Operations, Business Operations or Commercial Strategy within a high-growth technology, SaaS, marketplace or digital consumer business.
Demonstrated success building marketing planning processes, operating models and organisational rhythms from the ground up.
Experience leading annual planning, quarterly business reviews, integrated launch planning and cross-functional programme management.
Strong commercial acumen with the ability to connect marketing activity to business outcomes and financial performance.
Excellent analytical capability, including experience developing KPIs, dashboards, measurement frameworks and executive reporting.
Deep understanding of modern marketing organisations across Brand, Growth, Product Marketing and Creative functions.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive alignment across complex global organisations.
Exceptional organisational and programme management skills, with the ability to manage multiple strategic initiatives simultaneously.
Experience managing budgets, agency relationships and cross-functional investment planning.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity and building new capabilities within fast-changing environments.
Strong communication, facilitation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate strategy into clear action.
Passion for music, creators and the independent artist ecosystem is highly desirable.
Experience supporting international or multi-market marketing organisations is preferred.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience; postgraduate qualification in Business, Marketing or Strategy is advantageous.
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred
Location: This role will be based out of the London, Believe office in Kings Cross. TuneCore operates on an in-office and remote hybrid model giving our teams flexibility and choice of how they work. Required in-office Tues, Weds, Thurs.
 Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.
 Additional Information
 Our Values
TuneCore is a team of creators, for creators. Our mission is to support our artists and labels at every stage of their careers. Our driving forces are fairness, expertise, respect and transparency. As global citizens, we believe that if we build more diverse, equitable and inclusive teams across our company, we will collectively create and offer more innovative solutions and better serve our artists, labels, partners, and employees. 
 We strive to build a company that reflects the communities we serve and embraces the diversity of the world we live in, where each person’s unique perspective is valued, and where everyone has the same opportunities and is supported in their personal and professional growth. From our hiring practices to the culture we create and nurture, we are committed to listening, learning and evolving. Our goal is to make TuneCore an inspirational place that feels comfortable and familiar no matter how you look, where you call home, who you love, what you believe, or what’s on your playlist. 
 CSR Strategy: Shaping Music for Good 
Our core values are put into action through Shaping Music for Good, Believe and TuneCore’s global corporate social responsibility strategy, integrated at all levels of the company and at the heart of our business model. 
 We strive to shape the music industry for good by building trusting relationships with artists and partners, investing in the growth and talent development of our local markets, and empowering our community to positively impact society. We work to achieve progress on our core priorities: gender equity, diversity, equity & inclusion, environmental sustainability, and wellness for our employees, artists, and industry partners. 
 Shapers Program 
Employees have the opportunity to join the Shapers Program, a resource group made up of teammates who want to dedicate their time and skills to Shaping Music For Good initiatives. Shapers develop action plans, educate teammates, support the implementation of programs, and inspire action within the organization on causes and issues that align with TuneCore and Believe’s SMFG priorities. 
 Inclusion in the Music Business Report
In 2025, Believe and TuneCore partnered with the Annenberg Inclusion Initiative, the world’s leading think tank studying diversity and inclusion in the entertainment industry, to produce the second Inclusion in the Music Business report which analyzes the gender, race, and ethnicity among executive leadership in the music industry.

 Benefits & Perks
At TuneCore we’re committed to the well-being of our employees and aim to create a workplace that fosters both personal and professional growth. Our inclusive benefits include, but are not limited to:

Coordinating the planning and delivery of marketing campaigns, product launches, and business initiatives.
Working with cross-functional teams to execute impactful multi-channel marketing activity.
Aligning campaign plans with commercial objectives and customer growth opportunities.
Maintaining campaign briefs, timelines, workflows, and delivery updates.
Driving continuous improvements to campaign planning processes and ways of working.
Developing supplier-funded marketing proposals to unlock additional investment.
Managing campaign administration and performance reporting.

Experience supporting the planning and delivery of marketing campaigns or commercial projects within a fast-paced environment.

Commercial awareness, with the ability to understand business objectives and support campaigns that drive customer engagement and sales performance.
